key_insight: Process-zone condensation preserves full-discretization accuracy without training while the eliminated region of the composite cell remains elastic.
engineering_relevance: The method can accelerate FE² simulations of composites with fibre–matrix debonding and matrix plasticity, but gains depend on material and process-zone size.
method: Eliminate the linear elastic cell remainder using a Schur complement, retaining interface and process-zone internal variables.
Recover macroscopic stress and consistent tangent through influence matrices.
Check the eliminated region by back-substitution each increment and expand the retained zone when needed.
evidence_signal: Eight of nine 2D paths matched full-cell stress and tangent to 1e-11; 2D path timings yielded a 3.3× aggregate speed-up excluding setup and checks, while adaptive plate simulations were 1.51× faster for glass/polypropylene but slower for glass/epoxy.
watch_item: Exactness requires the eliminated region to remain elastic; zone expansion, active-set changes and adaptation costs can erase speed gains, as in the certified 3D cases.
paper_title: Process-zone condensation: a discretization-exact reduced cell model for FE$^2$ analysis of composites with fibre-matrix debonding and matrix plasticity
